# Shared infrastructure against excavation plans and dated contexts

We find a townscape in which streets, drains and entrances could follow different histories. Farmana's plans preserve lane sections beside additions to houses and a capped building passage. Harappa's gateway sequence combines restricted access with a continuing drainage connection. Dholavira's gates combine older masonry with later blocking. These observations support the possibility that connected services persisted while access changed locally. They also challenge any version of the shared-infrastructure idea that requires every route to remain open.

The measured plans and documentary contexts do not yet decide whether common rules, central supervision, engineering constraints or repeated household decisions produced that pattern. Our fixed six-town source audit assembled no complete comparison of street persistence against internal partition persistence, and no matched pair joining documentary use to an independently dated repair. Those quantities remain unknown. We have tested the published evidence's geometry, sequence and ability to support the proposed causal comparison, and we report the failed joins alongside the positive ones.

## What we tested

C-0017 proposes that building groups changed their houses under rules that preserved connected routes and services. Its first prediction compares the fraction of shared-route boundaries retained through rebuilding with the fraction of internal partitions retained in the same excavated area. C-0018 connects sealings with changes in custody between groups. C-0019 extends serial tablet administration to obligations for shared work. The last proposal has an existing credence of 0.10 and requires physical evidence that distinguishes work from ordinary goods allocation.

We froze `PROTOCOL.md` before new measurement. Farmana, Kanmer, Banawali, Harappa, Dholavira and Lothal remained in the primary source frame even when their plans proved unsuitable for a persistence comparison. A dated amendment added Mohenjo-daro as a supplementary test of source availability and measurement, without replacing a failed town. Architectural inventories were saved before the new documentary overlays were read. The context module was frozen before its coder received the new architectural outcomes. Earlier published examples were already familiar, so this separation reduces one source of fitting without creating a fresh confirmation sample.

The results register preserves source titles, editions, hashes, page and figure locators, relative phases, scale, north references, reading bounds and reasons for missing fields. Full reports, source images, detailed traces and illustrated products remain local on D:. The new study does not alter the earlier comparison, conjecture credences or the shared benchmark spending record. The versioned synthetic shots result checks workflow guards; it supplies no archaeological score.

## The plans support selective continuity

Farmana gives the clearest bounded illustration of local change. In the eastern Period IIA plan, a single section of Lane 1 measures 1.913 m, with a conditional reading range of 1.783–2.047 m. Lane 2 measures 1.953 m, range 1.822–2.087 m. A section of Main Street measures 3.961 m, range 3.700–4.229 m. These are particular sections of drawn masonry. The report's 1.6 m average for Lane 1 describes a different scope, and that difference remains unresolved rather than being averaged away. The excavators place a bathing platform at Lane 1's exposed end and infer earlier disuse; a later addition projects into Lane 2. Their local sequences include both retained alignment and encroachment.

In the central Period IIB area, Structure 3I gained an eastern buttress. Its drawn projection measures 0.595 m, with a reading range of 0.250–0.949 m, which includes the report's 0.55 m. Two passages give conflicting lengths for that addition, 1.00 m and 2.10 m. They remain one repair case with a source conflict. Passage 4C has a drawn clear width of 1.786 m, range 1.552–2.025 m, below its later northern cap. That cap closes the compound's connection with central Lane 1. The plan does not show closure of Lane 1 itself. These details matter because a town can preserve circulation past a building while withdrawing access into it. The eastern Lane 1 and central Lane 1 are separate named features in separate areas and phases. Source: Shinde, Osada and Kumar 2011, Chapter 5, Figures 5.18 and 5.70, pp. 57,99,103,117,145,152.

Harappa supplies an architectural contrast of the same kind. The Mound ET gateway was partly blocked by the late Period 3C Drain 51, while east–west circulation crossed above its culvert. The earlier drain had clogged; the sequence shows renewed drainage alongside changed access, rather than uninterrupted service. In a separate Area C setting, a local reading of the gateway opening on Kenoyer's composite Figure 4.15 is 2.878 m, range 2.378–3.407 m. That drawing combines gateway stages and cannot assign the width to every stage. We also registered the Area C cart-track and upper street plans, Figures 4.12 and 4.16, using excavation-grid controls independent of the walls. Registration succeeds geometrically, but the upper drawing combines street levels and the lower exposure lacks a comparable inventory of internal partitions. Consequently the intended persistence difference cannot be estimated from this pair.

Dholavira's plans show later blocks in gate passages, with mixed phases preserved in the drawings. Lothal's recovered Figure 17 allows readings of a Phase IV passage and a house entrance, but the held source set does not provide the corresponding complete earlier street network. Banawali's composite town plan and Kanmer's fort plan establish bounded design observations; their publication or excavation updates cannot substitute for occupation phases. Each town remains visible in the coverage table.

Mohenjo-daro provides four readable local chords across First Street in Mackay's successive plans. Their estimates are 7.34,7.89,8.17 and 10.26 m, with broad reading ranges. These sections sit beside different local frontages and are not the same registered ground transect. The fifth frozen section remains unmeasurable because no continuous western bank can be identified at that row. The result establishes the availability of repeated street drawings and measurable local geometry. It supplies neither a street-widening trend nor a count of independent rebuilding episodes. Our independent visual audit confirms the selected 0–50-foot scale marks and retains both plausible edges on Plate XIX.

## The strongest documentary joins have different functions

Harappa's Trench 54 courtyard ties tablet manufacture to a bounded architectural setting. The plan labels workshop 601, walls, stairs and a platform; unfinished and broken tablets occur with production waste. Other Harappa objects have positive room, floor or sump associations. The jar H95-2661/6640-501 was reused in a floor as a sump, giving an operating context for the installed vessel while leaving the earlier inscription events distinct. These observations locate activities more precisely than a site name. Manufacture, later possession and final disposal still require separate histories.

The 22-tablet group near Wall 296 is a counterexample to reading a concentration as an office. Sixteen tablets formed a reconstructed clump, two lay nearby and four were scattered. The source identifies secondary deposition after the wall was built. Its map locates discarded material; it does not locate the original administrative use. Banawali's horned-tiger seal in a paved sitting room offers a more direct household association, although its registration, subphase and dated building event remain unresolved.

A cross-module check after the context freeze found a positive Kanmer floor association in the already held annual-report preview. The report places a terracotta sealing in the southwest corner of grid Z28 on floor levels of layer 9, and separately a button-shaped steatite seal in X30, layer 8. Neither has a registration, exact room or independent date in that passage. `POSTJOIN-LEAD-01.json` preserves the source text format and page locator without adding these mentions to the frozen 32 assessments or identifying them with the three-impression cohort. The lead improves the next field-register request.

Lothal preserves fastening contacts on sealings and a warehouse-associated concentration. Physical traces can distinguish contact with cords, containers or fixed fastenings. They do not independently identify a handover, recipient or labour obligation. Its passage deposit also admits competing formation histories involving discard and fire or collapse. The 93 rows in Frenez and Tosi's Table 1 contain W=35, W1=18, W2=11, O=10 and ?=19, reproduced by a separate visual recount. Their prose gives O=11 and ?=17 and sums to 92. W1 locations depend on stamp similarity, while W2 gives a broad trench. Both cannot be treated as independently observed warehouse findspots in a test using stamp similarity.

Dholavira's fallen ten-sign inlays join writing to the western chamber of the Castle north gate. The original overhead mounting is a reconstruction, and its installation date is unresolved. Three of the 225 context-table rows explicitly name rooms; those leads deserve excavation-record recovery. The table supplies no demonstrated original-use-to-repair chain. The field counts describe what the table records, not how often primary contexts existed in the ancient town.

## Dates change the interpretation of apparent joins

The audit preserves 78 source-specific dating entries, including 76 entries with a reported radiocarbon determination or thermoluminescence result. Repeated publications and paired laboratory methods do not automatically add independent specimens. Two further entries preserve calibrated ages for intrusive Kanmer rice without inventing raw determinations omitted from the paragraph. No pooled calendar model was fitted.

Harappa's hearths below Wall 15 provide actual stratigraphic dating evidence. The excavation report infers construction after about 2470 BC, but the tablet association conflicts: the Trench 22 prose places two faience tablets inside the wall, while their Figure 11 captions say Trench 7/8, wash. Choosing the prose alone would manufacture the desired architectural join. Lothal's dated posthole above Phase IV flood debris and an ashy layer sealing a Phase IIIB wall provide other partial sample-to-feature chains, all outside the warehouse sealing deposit.

Two direct checks defeat tempting transfers of a nearby date. Farmana's PLD-12422 carries a Trench 1E1/Structure 3N label yet dates to AD 616–666 at the source's 95.4% calibrated coverage. Kanmer's PLD-16351 and PLD-16353 rice dates fall in the fourth–fifth centuries AD despite Harappan field associations; the source discusses reworking or percolation. These are positive evidence of intrusion or later activity, and they prevent us from using a structure name or cultural phase as the date of a seal's use.

## What this changes

The study replaces a town-level resemblance argument with named, auditable architectural and depositional cases. It adds measured plan geometry, one limited registration, explicit contradictions and primary-source dates. The central numerical prediction of preferential route persistence remains unestimated because the required comparable excavation windows are absent. The documentary predictions remain below their entry requirements because the object, operating deposit, building episode and independent date do not form a complete matched chain.

The strongest reading supported here is selective continuity: connected urban services could continue through local rebuilding while thresholds, entrances and access changed. Common rules remain a viable explanation, and their institutional cause is open. The deciding test is a new, sufficiently powered comparison of fully exposed, phase-joined routes and internal partitions with preservation held comparable, followed by documentary contexts dated independently of the connection being tested. If the apparent advantage of shared routes disappears under those controls, or if the seal and tablet relation is generated by manufacture and secondary disposal, the corresponding shared-infrastructure claims fail.

# Measurements and context joins

The frozen register contains 18 plan quantities, 29 architectural source cases, 32 context assessments and 78 dating entries. The six primary towns remain in the frame; Mohenjo-daro is a supplementary availability control. The 42 source-use records include repeated use of the same publications and 35 distinct recorded payload hashes. These are separate denominators.

## Local plan readings

All ranges are conditional reading-sensitivity bounds. They cover the saved endpoint and scale choices; unknown original survey error is additional. The complete feature names, phase attribution, source locators and north references remain in run-v1.json and the module tables.

The residuals quantify fit to the printed grid, not original survey accuracy or certification of comparable exposure. Both drawings retain unknown compilation and scan errors.

## Prediction entry results

| Prediction | Qualified units and effect | Result |
|---|---|---|
| C-0017 P1 | 0; effect unknown | not estimable: No source pair supplies comparable complete route and partition inventories, despite one grid-registered descriptive pair. |
| C-0017 P2 | 0; effect unknown | entry gate unmet: Local additions and service continuities lack the complete matched component and repair design; a visible addition is not a qualified P2 unit. |
| C-0017 P3 | 0; effect unknown | not estimable: No jointly assembled dated repair-network panel. Reported sample determinations remain separate from event dates. |
| C-0018 | 0; effect unknown | entry gate unmet: Registered object or adjudicated cohort in a demonstrated original-use or custody context, independently dated against a named construction or repair, then paired with a matched episode. |
| C-0019 | 0; effect unknown | entry gate unmet: No qualified work-allocation pair; text contents and labour meanings are unassigned. |


## The source cases have different denominators

The architectural records are authored assessments of named sequences or source limitations. Repeated prose, plan and photograph views of one addition remain one source-event group where the module can establish that identity. They are not all independent rebuilding episodes. The 18 quantities below comprise 17 lengths and one angle, including a check of a source-labelled robber-trench width. They are readings of published drawings, not new excavation surveys.

The independent arithmetic review recomputes all 18 quantities, the alternative Mackay edge and both grid fits. A separate reader inspected the Mackay scale marks and street banks. The saved reading bounds allow uncertain endpoint and scale-bar selection. Original survey error, scan distortion, line generalisation and uncertain phase combination remain additional errors without quantified distributions.

### Farmana, Kanmer and Banawali

Farmana's eastern IIA plan and central IIB plan permit local dimensions with explicit source phase assignments. The two Lane 1 labels refer to different areas. Figures 5.69 and 5.70 are western and eastern halves of the same IIB plan, so treating them as successive occupations would create artificial retention. The northern cap of compound passage 4C cuts its link to central Lane 1; the source leaves the lane open in the mapped area. Structure 3I's eastern addition has conflicting reported lengths of 1.00 m and 2.10 m, retained within one event group. Its width reading uses an interpreted original face and therefore carries a larger endpoint radius.

Kanmer's northeastern fort corner gives an angle of 88.532 degrees with a reading bound 77.810–99.254 degrees. Its short exposed arms limit precision. The printed ratio 2 cm = 5 m lacks a usable graphic bar for scale after scan resizing, so no metric wall length is reported. Counts of partly exposed rooms and structural phases remain tied to their trenches and reports rather than being multiplied into town-wide buildings.

Banawali's composite plan and the reports of a changed interior inside an inherited outline remain useful qualitative evidence. The 1983–84 and 1987–88 publications update exposure, not successive ancient occupation plans. A proposed angle was withdrawn during visual review because one selected segment lay above a curving defence band. Its original clicks and withdrawal reason remain local; no corrected angle was substituted after seeing the outcome.

### Harappa, Dholavira and Lothal

Harappa Area C, Kenoyer 1991 Figures 4.12 and 4.16, is the one grid-registered descriptive pair. Six grid controls fit each drawing; two further points per drawing were held out. The fit errors and held-out errors appear below. The registration uses no archaeological walls as controls and no flexible warp. Its common geometric window does not certify common phase exposure: the early plan exposes a narrow strip of cart tracks and the upper drawing combines street levels and encroachment. The separate HARP Trench 39N image combines Period 3B drainage and Period 3C masonry. No internal-wall denominator is available in the lower window.

Harappa's Mound ET gateway and Drain 51 sequence retains the distinction between service, passage and entry. The robber-trench reading is a useful calibration check because the report labels its width 2.18 m; it is not a street or a preserved partition. In Trench 54, robbing and later disturbance remain visible limits on any comparison of surviving masonry.

Dholavira's east and north gates show later blocks in composite plans. Their local clearances cannot date those blocks. The original East Gate north arrow points right; its selected display crop rotates 90 degrees counterclockwise to put north upward. The North Gate and well-and-tank plans have north downward. Each transformation is recorded, and none establishes true versus magnetic north. The well's drawn horizontal diameter 3.797 m differs in scope and drawing precision from the prose dimensions 4.00 m east–west and 4.25 m north–south. Both records remain available.

Lothal Figure 17 was recovered inside the held text scan after the separately requested plate set proved incomplete. It gives a Phase IV plan of Block B with named houses, passage and entrance. That recovery changes local measurement coverage but does not recover the complete earlier street network. The warehouse-associated sealing deposit has its own discovery-area plan and competing interpretations involving discard or destruction, separately mapped in the atlas.

### Mohenjo-daro as an availability control

Mackay's Plates XVI–XX preserve five relative plan states, the last combining Late Ia and II. The first rendering pass misread the scan's alternating plan and blank-back sequence; its failed renders remain local. The corrected page indices are 45,47,49,51,53. Four local First Street chords can be read and one cannot. Plate XIX retains an alternative western edge, whose estimate and combined sensitivity bounds accompany the primary reading. Different frontages, source compilation and an unmeasurable fifth chord prevent a chronological widening claim.

The acquired Green, Alam and Petrie 2026 supplement contains summary statistics and code, but no street vectors or individual house polygons. It recovers published 80% intervals for five DK-GS residential-area Ginis. Their assigned centuries belong to a published model, not independent dates for street repairs. The atlas uses them only to show the distinction between an available summary and the missing feature-level comparison. Repeated houses across phases must not be summed as independent households. The source's DGN decimal conflict between prose and table remains preserved in the earlier package.

## Positive contexts and broken date chains

The context assessments retain object or cohort identity, material, formation, deposit, named feature, phase, dating evidence and source locator. A cohort and one of its individual members can both be assessed; 32 assessments therefore do not mean 32 objects or independent use events. The source records below distinguish manufacture, original operation, reuse and secondary deposition without assigning sign meanings.

A post-freeze review adds one Kanmer lead separately: OP10 printed p. 86, preview page 94, reports a terracotta sealing in the southwest corner of Z28 on floor levels of layer 9, and separately a button-shaped steatite seal in X30, layer 8. The source is held as gzip-compressed JSONP text, with directly mapped private-use digit glyphs; no page image or full PDF was acquired. Missing registration, exact room, use-event relation and independent date prevent a qualified pair. Neither mention is identified with the three-impression cohort. The source hash and exact handling are in POSTJOIN-LEAD-01.json; run-v1's32 assessments are unchanged.

| Context | Positive observation | Link still missing |
|---|---|---|
| Harappa Trench 54, workshop 601 | Registered tablet illustration units occur with production debris in a bounded courtyard setting | A dated sequence joining construction or repair to documentary use; subsequent recipients and function |
| Harappa Trench 10E seals | Named room floor and courtyard floor/fill associations | Event-specific stratigraphy and independent repair chronology |
| Harappa Trench 9 jar H95-2661/6640-501 | Inscribed vessel reused as an installed floor sump | Dates of its separate inscription, use and installation events |
| Harappa Wall 296 tablets | A mapped 22-tablet group, including a 16-item clump | Original manufacture and use locations; deposition is secondary and later than wall construction |
| Harappa Wall 15 | Actual hearth determinations below the wall | Tablet provenience conflict between prose and caption; no dated pair joining repair and use |
| Banawali sitting room | Horned-tiger seal reported in a mud-brick-paved room | Verified registration, house subphase and independently related sample |
| Farmana S1–S6 | Named phases, areas, object types and some fastening or suspension contacts | Explicitly qualified structural associations and event-specific dates |
| Kanmer three impressions | Repeated-stamp perforated objects with published functional proposals | Held full object-to-room register and dated use context |
| Dholavira gate inlays | Ten-sign material fallen in a named gate chamber | Original mounting and emplacement date |
| Lothal sealings | Physical fastening contacts and mapped concentration | Primary application-to-deposit history, independently coded custody change and event date |

Harappa's Table 1 reports Wall 15's underlying hearth samples A-8047/AA-16461,A-8048 and A-8049. The source's first-sigma calendar ranges remain source-specific; A-8049 is flagged aberrant. The text's construction-after-about 2470 BC inference does not date the two faience tablets whose Figure 11.4/.6 captions identify Trench 7/8, wash while the prose discusses Trench 22. A laboratory date, a sample and a wall association are distinct steps, all recorded separately.

Farmana's dating appendix provides 26 AMS entries, predominantly wood, including later Gupta and Medieval material. PLD-12422 is 1390±20 BP and AD 616–666 at the source's 95.4% coverage despite its Structure 3N label. Kanmer's genuine radiocarbon publications preserve 16 AMS and nine conventional results, with repeated lab IDs and source differences kept separate. The two intrusive-rice entries retain their source-reported fourth–fifth-century AD ages. A held file named kanmer2013.pdf proves to be publisher HTML and is excluded as an unavailable full-paper route.

Lothal's six charcoal determinations name trenches, loci, depths and deposits. TF-23 relates to a mud-wall posthole above Phase IV flood debris;TF-22 comes from an ashy layer sealing Phase IIIB flood debris and a wall. None dates the SRG3 warehouse sealing deposit. Parenthesized ages in the 1963 paper use another half-life convention rather than a modern calibrated confidence interval. Dholavira's reported TL ages are broad and lack the sample-to-target-feature relation needed here. No calibrated ages were recomputed or pooled.

## Coverage and source conflicts

Dholavira's 225 inherited context rows retain 225 unique accession strings, pending physical-object identity adjudication. The usable-label predicate finds 211 stratum labels, 201 depth labels and three explicit room labels. It excludes the literal marker Unst.; counting that marker produces 213/202 instead. The separate clarification preserves the frozen data and corrects an interim explanation. Stage, pit, room and disturbed flags can overlap; they are neither percentages of primary use nor a completeness score for excavation.

The Lothal recount independently reproduces all 93 literal provenance rows. W1 is inferred by stamp comparison and W2 supplies the broad SRG3 trench, while W records the reported warehouse association. Table W35/W1=18/W2=11/O10/?19 differs from prose W35/W1=18/W2=11/O11/?17. The table denominator 93, prose category sum 92, and older 65/69-of-90 populations remain separate. No count is silently reconciled into a new physical-object total.

## What the entry audit decides

The numerical persistence effect and documentary odds ratios remain null in the results register. The present source frame has zero fully qualified persistence episodes and zero matched documentary pairs under the frozen design. Single dimensions, multiple laboratory entries and many catalogue rows cannot replace those independent units. This is a completed evidence and measurement pilot; the institutional hypotheses await the new joined data specified in TEST-DESIGN.md.

The strongest reading is selective continuity: connected services could remain usable while local access and buildings changed. The deciding test is a preservation-controlled comparison of complete phase windows with independently dated operational documentary contexts. Loss of the route advantage under those controls, or a documentary association wholly explained by manufacture and discard, defeats the relevant extension.

# The strongest reading and the deciding test

The plans support selective continuity of connected services through local architectural change. Farmana's capped compound passage and Harappa's partly blocked gateway show why street alignment, through-access, entry into a building and drainage must be measured separately. A drain can continue while a threshold closes. The published evidence makes continued coordination plausible, but it does not identify the institution that maintained it.

Writing participated in several spatially distinct activities. Harappa has bounded tablet manufacture and positive room, floor and sump associations. Lothal has physical fastening evidence and a concentrated later deposit. Dholavira has a gate-chamber inscription. A model of urban administration should explain that variety. The specific proposal that tablets recorded shared-work obligations still lacks a physical distinction from goods allocation.

We retain the existing exploratory credences: C-0017 at 0.55, C-0018 at 0.35 and C-0019 at 0.10. Reusing their published examples does not supply the new confirmation evidence required by their update rules. The zero qualified episode and matched-pair counts describe this source audit's eligibility, while the architectural sequences and documentary activities are positive observations in their own right.

## A comparison that can decide the architectural claim

Recover complete phase drawings, excavation records and sections for at least twelve independent rebuilding episodes in four towns. That is an entry minimum, with final sample size determined by a pilot that models missing exposure, preservation and town dependence. Before measuring persistence, freeze the common excavation windows and inventory every visible shared-route boundary, service line and internal partition. Use independent survey controls for registration. Match material, foundation depth, robbing and excavation exposure, and retain unknown features separately from removed ones.

The frozen target remains a retained fraction for shared routes at least 0.25 above the fraction for internal partitions, with an interval calibrated for the small number of towns that excludes zero. A powered result with no preferential continuity would defeat C-0017's core claim. If apparent continuity disappears when composite phases or restoration are removed, the corresponding examples fail even before a population-level comparison. Six directly joined repairs in three towns can then test whether locally different components still made usable connections. Independent construction dates must determine whether repairs group by connected infrastructure better than by proximity and engineering constraints.

## A comparison that can decide the documentary extension

The next useful unit is a registered object or adjudicated cohort on a demonstrable operating surface or fastening, related stratigraphically to a named construction or repair. Short-lived samples must bracket that event, and the object-use relation must be established separately from final deposition. The immediate recovery targets are Harappa's named floor and courtyard seals, Trench 54's production sequence, the conflicting Wall 15 tablet proveniences, Banawali's sitting room and Dholavira's explicitly named rooms. Lothal requires resolution of deposit formation as well as its provenance counts.

Freeze custody-change settings from physical handling sequences and independently justified access, storage and wear evidence before reading sealing occurrence. A gate, storeroom or threshold alone supplies a candidate setting, not evidence of a change in custody. The pilot must establish a reproducible physical criterion for that change without using the occurrence or interpreted meaning of the documentary objects being tested. Twenty matched context pairs in four towns are an entry minimum, subject to demonstrated sensitivity. C-0018 requires an odds ratio of at least two, an appropriate cluster interval above one and a relation that survives restriction to primary use. If adequately recovered household possession, manufacture and discard explain the distribution without a custody-change association, the handover claim fails. A repeated legend cannot repair a failed physical prediction.

C-0019 needs an additional distinction: evidence that the relevant records concern work rather than ordinary movable goods. Residues, direct provisioning associations, wear and an independently defined repair schedule are candidate evidence. Provisioning alone also fits goods allocation, so the pilot must demonstrate an observable distinction specific to work before inscription units are scored. If the varying series instead track goods classes that explain their variation and defeat the shared-work prediction, abandon the labour-specific claim. A new confirmation round must freeze identities, aliases, production groups, features and scoring on discovery material, pass the benchmark's exposure audit, and receive one joint update for overlapping observations.

Our strongest reading is that connected services outlasted some local uses and entrances. The decisive observation would be a replicated, preservation-controlled advantage in route continuity, joined to independently dated operational documents. Its disappearance, or a distribution fully explained by workshops and secondary dumps, would disprove the corresponding extension of the shared-infrastructure idea.

# The next discriminating comparison

Status: prospective acquisition design informed by this exposed pilot. This file does not register a fresh confirmation round. The core pass rules are inherited from C-0017 to C-0019 and the frozen protocol; final variance, sample size, scoring family and power require a blinded pilot on new admissible material.

## Recover the missing observation

For architecture, request the original phase drawings, survey grid and section sheets for a complete bounded building group and its connecting street or drain. Harappa's published Area C cart-track and upper street plans, Kenoyer 1991 Figures 4.12 and 4.16, show that independent grid registration can be feasible, while their narrow early exposure and combined upper levels show why geometric alignment alone cannot qualify the comparison. A complete later plan cannot repair an incomplete earlier window. Farmana's central Figures 5.69 and 5.70 are adjacent halves of one Period IIB plan and must remain a single phase rather than a fabricated before-and-after pair.

For documentary contexts, recover field registration, lot, locus, level and section references before assigning objects to buildings. Resolve the Harappa Wall 15 conflict between caption and prose against the field register rather than voting between printed passages. Recover the individual find records for the Trench 10E seals and Trench 54 tablets. At Banawali, find the sitting-room seal's registration and the house's structural subphases. At Dholavira, follow the three literal room labels into a room-specific floor sequence. A site or broad stage does not meet these requests.

For dating, require a sample's material identification, laboratory determination, pretreatment, calibration convention and the physical relation between the sample and the target event. Prefer short-lived material where available. Preserve all stratigraphically inconsistent results for an explicit residuality or intrusion assessment. A Bayesian sequence model can combine independently justified order and dates; it cannot create an object-to-event association absent from the excavation record.

## Distinguish the competing explanations

| Explanation | Observation it predicts | Observation that would weaken it |
|---|---|---|
| Common rules for connected services | Preferential route continuity after matched preservation; usable joins across locally different construction | No continuity advantage in a powered comparison; joins exist only in composite drawings |
| Settlement-wide supervision | Repair timing and component choices follow settlement-wide coordination beyond engineering constraints | Stable local differences and staggered repairs cluster by connected groups with better withheld prediction |
| Engineering constraints | Slope, flow, load, foundation and flood exposure account for retained alignments and repairs | Connected-group prediction improves on those measured variables in new episode groups |
| Household decisions with inherited streets | Local additions and closures accumulate while movement follows inherited constraints | Preferential joined repairs and independent cross-group timing remain after those constraints are controlled |
| Workshop or secondary-discard concentration | Tablet and sealing association follows production waste and deposition rather than operational custody settings | Primary fastening and use contexts retain an association under matched recovery and independent custody coding |
| Goods allocation | Physical goods classes explain documentary variation | Work-specific associations and externally established repair or provision classes predict new records beyond goods and style |

These alternatives can coexist. The test compares their predictions for the same units and does not assign an institution from a plan's regularity alone. Local construction differences by themselves cannot distinguish negotiation from delegated supervision.

## Freeze and score

1. Adjudicate physical identity, aliases, faces, impressions of one stamp and copied production series. Split discovery and confirmation at the relevant dependent group, preserving exposure history. Previously examined plans and objects remain discovery evidence.
2. Have architectural coders inventory a complete common window before receiving documentary finds. Use source grid controls independent of the tested features. Report control fit, held-out control error, transformation and source survey uncertainty. Do not warp a plan until the desired walls coincide.
3. Have context coders identify original operation, manufacture, reuse, destruction and later discard before receiving the architecture persistence result. Record sediment volume, recovery method and preservation for both members of every candidate pair. A gateway or storage room supplies a candidate setting; the discovery pilot must validate a physical custody-change criterion independently of the tested sealing occurrence. Ordinary provisioning also fits goods allocation. Require an additional observable distinction specific to work before creating labour labels.
4. Establish episode chronology from independent physical stratigraphy and samples. Separate laboratory replicates, one specimen, one deposit and one rebuilding event. Freeze a chronological model before using it to label the tested repairs.
5. Use the discovery pilot to simulate the intended clustered design across plausible missingness and measurement-error scenarios. Freeze a sample size with adequate sensitivity to the inherited 0.25 route difference and odds ratio of two. The minima of twelve episodes and twenty pairs do not certify power.
6. Freeze all registered participants, target measures, exclusion rules, influence checks and the one joint update for overlapping predictions. Run the actual benchmark only after its fresh-population and spent-family checks pass. Read confirmation once.

## Record a result that can fail

Publish retained, changed, removed and unobservable features with their source coordinates and reasons. Report the eligible denominator before the effect. For the architectural target, calculate shared-route minus internal-partition persistence within common windows and retain the town-level dependence. For documentary targets, report matched recovery denominators and the primary-use subset. Leave unestimable effects null rather than returning zero.

The strongest model consistent with this pilot is selective continuity of services through changing local access. It survives only if new fully joined evidence retains that preference after preservation and engineering controls. A powered absence of preferential continuity, or a documentary association produced entirely by manufacture and redeposition, decides against the relevant claim.
